items.title: Introduce Repository and Unit of Work for incremental lead-outreach persistence
acceptance: Lead outreach domain depends on a repository port rather than the MySQL driver
Pending insert and multi-row completion use row-level incremental SQL instead of persistAll
Social and email completion are atomic and rollback on any failure
Unique-key races and optimistic status conflicts fail without duplicate side effects
Memory and MySQL adapters follow the same repository contract
Public API, tenant scope, security gates, and existing business behavior do not regress
nonGoals: No production database or SMTP call
No public API or frontend change
No migration of unrelated domains in this loop

items.title: Persist LangGraph workflow state, approvals, effects, and audit in MySQL
acceptance: A second engine instance can recover an awaiting workflow from MySQL
Resume validates actor and tenant and rechecks authorization before effects
Concurrent approvals and replay execute the business effect once
Checkpoint, run, approval, effect, and audit persistence reject secrets
MySQL writes are row-level, parameterized, recoverable, and never full-table replacement
Public API, security, E2E, and dependency gates do not regress
nonGoals: No real model or production credential
No public AI route or frontend UI

items.title: Encrypt model and lead-source credentials through SecretVault
acceptance: Model and lead-source API keys are never stored as plaintext in MySQL
Legacy plaintext can migrate with checkpoints and repeated migration preserves data
Damaged ciphertext, unknown or revoked keys, and cross-tenant context decryption fail without plaintext fallback
Primary-key rotation, transitional decryption keys, consistent masking, and production startup gates are supported
Logs, errors, and API responses never expose complete keys; real KMS and supplier outbound calls remain zero
nonGoals: No real cloud KMS or HSM integration
No real model or lead-source credentials
No new public API or frontend page
